lessons.claim: The direct thermodynamic stress of a many-body system with interaction forces is the force moment (1/V)*sum_alpha F_i^alpha x_j^alpha (= the virial / force dipole). Brownian motion is replaced exactly by the effective force F_Br = -kT grad ln P_N, and sum F_Br = 0. ★ The grounds for actually being able to compute the stress in BD code. But adding the instantaneous value of the random force straight into the virial double-counts with F_Br, so it has to be confirmed by comparison against a kT=0 deterministic run

not_verified: whether it double-counts has not yet been confirmed by execution
